entries.content_plain:
CHAPTER 26
 
De 26:1-15. The Confession of Him That Offers the Basket of First Fruits.

2. Thou shalt take of the first of all the fruit of the earth--The Israelites in Canaan, being God's tenants-at-will, were required to give Him tribute in the form of first-fruits and tithes. No Israelite was at liberty to use any productions of his field until he had presented the required offerings. The tribute began to be exigible after the settlement in the promised land, and it was yearly repeated at one of the great feasts (Le 2:14; 23:10; 23:15; Nu 28:26; De 16:9). Every master of a family carried it on his shoulders in a little basket of osier, peeled willow, or palm leaves, and brought it to the sanctuary.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1872"/><div sID="gen2487" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1872"/><hi type="bold">5. thou shalt say ... A Syrian ready to perish was my father--</hi>rather, "a wandering Syrian." The ancestors of the Hebrews were nomad shepherds, either Syrians by birth as Abraham, or by long residence as Jacob. When they were established as a nation in the possession of the promised land, they were indebted to God's unmerited goodness for their distinguished privileges, and in token of gratitude they brought this basket of first-fruits. <div eID="gen2487" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1874"/><div sID="gen2489" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1874"/><hi type="bold">12-15. When thou hast made an end of tithing all the tithes of thine increase the third year--</hi>Among the Hebrews there were two tithings. The first was appropriated to the Levites (<reference osisRef="Num.18.21">Nu 18:21</reference>). The second, being the tenth of what remained, was brought to Jerusalem in kind; or it was converted into money, and the owner, on arriving in the capital, purchased sheep, bread, and oil (<reference osisRef="Deut.14.22">De 14:22</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.14.23">23</reference>). This was done for two consecutive years. But this second tithing was eaten at home, and the third year distributed among the poor of the place (<reference osisRef="Deut.14.28">De 14:28</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.14.29">29</reference>). <div eID="gen2489" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 12-15. When thou hast made an end of tithing all the tithes of thine increase the third year--Among the Hebrews there were two tithings. The first was appropriated to the Levites (Nu 18:21). The second, being the tenth of what remained, was brought to Jerusalem in kind; or it was converted into money, and the owner, on arriving in the capital, purchased sheep, bread, and oil (De 14:22, 23). This was done for two consecutive years. But this second tithing was eaten at home, and the third year distributed among the poor of the place (De 14:28, 29).
